What is the name and acronym of the agreement that makes Google Search the default on Apple products?

results.text: Apple is in court because of something called the Information Services Agreement, or ISA: a deal that makes Google’s search engine the default on Apple’s products. The ISA has been in place since 2002, but Cue was responsible for negotiating its current iteration with Google CEO Sundar Pichai in 2016. In testimony today, the Justice Department grilled Cue about the specifics of the deal.

metadata.title: Apple defends Google Search deal in court: ‘There wasn’t a valid alternative’
metadata.author: David Pierce

results.text: Cue was on the stand as a witness in US v. Google, the landmark antitrust trial over Google’s search business. Cue is one of the highest-profile witnesses in the case so far, in part because the deal between Google and Apple — which makes Google the default search engine on all Apple devices and pays Apple billions of dollars a year — is central to the US Department of Justice’s case against Google.

metadata.title: Apple defends Google Search deal in court: ‘There wasn’t a valid alternative’
metadata.author: David Pierce

results.text: Rosenberg explained how Google gets manufacturers to sign a mobile app distribution agreement (MADA) that requires Android smartphone makers (like Samsung or Oppo) to pre-load a bundle of 11 Google apps on the device, including Search, Chrome and Play. They don’t have to be the default choices, he said.

metadata.title: More from the US v Google trial: vertical search, pre-installs and the case of Firefox/Yahoo
metadata.author: Rebecca Bellan
